written.myAnswer: Observation provides information about a scientific problem and helps form a hypothesis. Experimentation tests the hypothesis; results indicate whether it is supported or should be rejected.
The basic steps are recognition of a scientific problem, observation, hypothesis, deduction, experimentation, and results.

Define the problem and observe and measure plant growth in shade and direct sunlight. Form the hypothesis that the species grows faster in shade, then deduce that shade-grown plants will show more growth if the hypothesis is correct. Grow similar plants under the two light conditions while controlling other factors, measure their growth over the same period, and compare the results. Use the direct-sunlight plants as the control group and the shade-grown plants as the experimental group; the results will show whether the observation is supported.
